chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which list correctly ranks these acids in order of increasing acidity (lowest pKa last)?

options.label: A
options.text: Trichloroacetic acid < Dichloroacetic acid < Chloroacetic acid < Acetic acid

options.label: B
options.text: Acetic acid < Chloroacetic acid < Dichloroacetic acid < Trichloroacetic acid

options.label: C
options.text: Acetic acid < Trichloroacetic acid < Chloroacetic acid < Dichloroacetic acid

options.label: D
options.text: Chloroacetic acid < Acetic acid < Trichloroacetic acid < Dichloroacetic acid

questions.correct_answer: Acetic acid < Chloroacetic acid < Dichloroacetic acid < Trichloroacetic acid
questions.explanation: Electronegative chlorine atoms stabilize the conjugate carboxylate base through inductive electron withdrawal.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.topic: Alcohol vs phenol vs carboxylic acid acidity
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders compounds from least acidic to most acidic?

options.label: A
options.text: Trifluoroacetic acid < Acetic acid < Phenol < Ethanol

options.label: B
options.text: Ethanol < Acetic acid < Phenol < Trifluoroacetic acid

options.label: C
options.text: Ethanol (pKa 16) < Phenol (pKa 10) < Acetic acid (pKa 4.75) < Trifluoroacetic acid (pKa 0.2)

options.label: D
options.text: Phenol < Ethanol < Acetic acid < Trifluoroacetic acid

questions.correct_answer: Ethanol (pKa 16) < Phenol (pKa 10) < Acetic acid (pKa 4.75) < Trifluoroacetic acid (pKa 0.2)
questions.explanation: Acidity increases as conjugate base stabilization increases: alkoxide < resonance-stabilized phenoxide < carboxylate < trifluorocarboxylate.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders hydrocarbons in increasing order of C-H acidity?

options.label: A
options.text: Ethane (sp3, pKa 50) < Ethylene (sp2, pKa 44) < Acetylene (sp, pKa 25)

questions.correct_answer: Ethane (sp3, pKa 50) < Ethylene (sp2, pKa 44) < Acetylene (sp, pKa 25)
questions.explanation: Higher s-character holds electrons closer to the nucleus, stabilizing the conjugate carbanion: sp3 (25% s) < sp2 (33% s) < sp (50% s).

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders substituted phenols in order of increasing acidity?
questions.explanation: Electron-donating methoxy deactivates phenoxide stability; electron-withdrawing nitro strongly stabilizes phenoxide by resonance.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders bases in order of increasing basicity in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Alkyl inductive donation enhances aliphatic amine basicity; aniline lone pair is delocalized into the aromatic ring.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.topic: Periodic trend in binary acid acidity
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders binary hydrides in order of increasing acidity across a period?
questions.explanation: Across a periodic row, electronegativity of the central atom increases, increasing conjugate base stability.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.topic: Binary halide acidity down a group
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders hydrogen halides in order of increasing acidity down a group?
questions.explanation: Down a group, bond strength decreases and halide ionic size increases, making HI the strongest acid (pKa -10).

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders chlorobutanoic acids in order of increasing acidity?
questions.explanation: Inductive electron withdrawal diminishes rapidly with distance from the carboxylate center.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders carbanions in order of increasing stability?

options.label: A
options.text: tert-Butyl carbanion < Methyl carbanion < Ethyl carbanion < Isopropyl carbanion

options.label: B
options.text: Ethyl carbanion < Methyl carbanion < tert-Butyl carbanion < Isopropyl carbanion

options.label: C
options.text: tert-Butyl carbanion < Isopropyl carbanion < Ethyl carbanion < Methyl carbanion

options.label: D
options.text: Methyl carbanion < Ethyl carbanion < Isopropyl carbanion < tert-Butyl carbanion

questions.correct_answer: tert-Butyl carbanion < Isopropyl carbanion < Ethyl carbanion < Methyl carbanion
questions.explanation: Alkyl groups donate electron density, destabilizing negatively charged carbanions: 3° < 2° < 1° < methyl.

questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders isomeric C5H12 pentanes in order of increasing boiling point?
questions.explanation: Linear unbranched alkanes have larger surface areas for London dispersion interactions, leading to higher boiling points.
